theme.vibe: warm desert adventure, curious and playful

cover.title: Velociraptor: The Feathered Hunter
cover.subtitle: A tiny dinosaur with a big surprise

narration.instructions: Warm, enthusiastic, and curious. Read like a favorite storyteller sharing an exciting discovery with a young child. Pause slightly between sentences.

pages.text: Have you ever seen a turkey? Velociraptor was about that size! It was not a giant monster. It was small, fast, and covered in feathers.
extras: Velociraptor weighed about as much as a big dog.

images.alt: Size comparison showing a Velociraptor next to a person -- the dinosaur only reaches up to the person's knee

pages.text: That's right -- Velociraptor had feathers! Scientists found bumps on its arm bones where feathers once attached. It looked more like a strange bird than a scaly lizard.

images.alt: Colorful illustration of a feathered Velociraptor standing in a natural pose

pages.text: But Velociraptor could not fly. Its arms were too short and its feathers were the wrong shape. So what were the feathers for? They kept it warm -- like a cozy coat! Look at this cassowary. It is a big bird alive today that has feathers but cannot fly, just like Velociraptor!
extras: Feathers may have helped attract mates, too.

images.alt: A cassowary, a modern bird that cannot fly and looks remarkably like a dinosaur, walking on the ground

pages.text: Look at this special claw! Velociraptor had a big, curved claw on each foot. It held this claw up off the ground to keep it sharp -- like a secret weapon.
extras: The claw was about as long as your finger.

images.alt: Model of a dromaeosaurid foot showing the raised sickle claw on the second toe

pages.text: Velociraptor used its claws and sharp teeth to catch small animals. It ate lizards, little mammals, and whatever else it could grab. What a fierce little hunter!

images.alt: A feathered Velociraptor catching a lizard in a sandy desert, shown in a playful child-friendly style

pages.text: Was Velociraptor smart? Yes! It had a big brain for its size -- about as smart as a hawk. That helped it be a clever hunter, but it could not solve puzzles like a parrot or a crow.
extras: Not as clever as the movies show!

images.alt: A clever-looking feathered Velociraptor with bright alert eyes, tilting its head as it observes its desert surroundings

pages.text: Velociraptor was FAST. Its name means 'swift thief.' It could run faster than the fastest person! Its long, stiff tail helped it balance and turn quickly.

images.alt: Complete Velociraptor skeleton showing its long legs and stiff tail built for speed

pages.text: Velociraptor lived in a hot, sandy desert -- not a green jungle like in the movies. Its home was in a place we now call Mongolia, far away in Asia.

images.alt: The Flaming Cliffs in Mongolia's Gobi Desert, with red-orange rock formations under a blue sky

pages.text: One amazing fossil shows a Velociraptor fighting a Protoceratops! They were buried together by a sandstorm millions of years ago. Scientists call it the Fighting Dinosaurs.
extras: This fossil is a national treasure of Mongolia.

images.alt: A feathered Velociraptor and a beaked Protoceratops facing off in a dramatic desert sandstorm

pages.text: Velociraptor had relatives big and small. Tiny Microraptor was the size of a crow. Huge Utahraptor was the size of a polar bear! They were all part of the same family.

images.alt: Size chart comparing dromaeosaurid dinosaurs from tiny Microraptor to enormous Utahraptor, with a human for scale

pages.text: Remember that turkey from the beginning? Birds are actually living dinosaurs! Every bird you see -- every robin, every chicken, every eagle -- is a relative of Velociraptor. Next time you see a bird, look closely. Can you spot the little dinosaur inside?

images.alt: A feathered Velociraptor standing next to a robin, a chicken, and an eagle, highlighting their family resemblance
